title: Docker networking: bridge, host and container-to-container traffic

videos.script: Every container has its own network. This lesson is about how those networks are wired together. {{bridge}} By default, each container gets a virtual cable to a bridge on the host, called docker zero. Containers there can reach each other by address, but not by name. {{user}} On a network you create, Docker runs a small DNS server, and names work. Different networks cannot see each other at all. {{localhost}} Then the question everybody asks: why does localhost inside a container not reach the machine? Because localhost is the container. And two modes that change that: host, with no walls, and none, with no network.
